description: Waits until a message arrives at an address — after you submit a sign-up form, say — and returns it with `extracted.codes` and `extracted.links`: verification codes and confirm links, most likely first. Without `after` it first looks back 2 minutes and returns the newest match from then, so a code that arrived before you called is not missed; narrow it with `from` (address or domain), `subject_contains`, or `has_code: "true"` so an earlier email is not mistaken for the one you want, and pass `after: "now"` to wait only for new mail. Answers `timed_out: true` after `timeout` seconds (default 50, at most 280); pass the returned `cursor` as `after` to keep waiting without missing anything. Most MCP clients give up on a call at 60 seconds, so keep each wait under that and chain them with `after`, unless you know your client allows longer. A matching message filed as spam is not returned: it is counted in `held_back` with its id, so check there before deciding nothing came, and pass `include_spam: "true"` to have it returned. Its text is cleaned by Pidgeon Firewall unless you pass `body: "original"`, as with `get_message`.

body.description: `clean` (default): hidden text removed and fake chat turns marked. `original`: as it arrived, with HTML.

name: await_message
title: Wait for the next message
